name: Swahili pronoun prefixes
explanation:
Conjugating verbs formula:

pronoun prefix + tense prefix + verb root

You can see this in action in the Tenses section below.

In Swahili, the subject is usually built into the verb. The pronoun tells you who is doing the action, and the verb prefix is the subject marker that attaches to the front of the verb.

cards.explanation: Mimi means "me" or "I". The matching verb prefix is ni-, as in ni + na + soma = ninasoma, "I am reading".
Wewe means "you" when speaking to one person. The matching verb prefix is u-, as in u + na + soma = unasoma, "you are reading".
Yeye means "he" or "she". The matching verb prefix is a-, as in a + na + soma = anasoma, "he/she is reading".
Sisi means "us" or "we". The matching verb prefix is tu-, as in tu + na + soma = tunasoma, "we are reading".
Ninyi means "you" when speaking to more than one person. The matching verb prefix is m-, as in m + na + soma = mnasoma, "you all are reading".
Wao means "they". The matching verb prefix is wa-, as in wa + na + soma = wanasoma, "they are reading".

cards.sw: subject prefix + tense prefix + verb root
cards.explanation: For many verb forms, build the verb from three pieces: who is acting, when it happens, and the action itself. Example: ni + na + soma = ninasoma, "I am reading".
The tense prefix -na- marks present or ongoing action. Combine it with the subject prefix and root: a + na + soma = anasoma, "he/she is reading".
